Title: Session-less requests are served as a global "dashboard Teacher" actor; unauthenticated GET returns cross-school support tickets
Evidence: `lib/iam.js:199-210` falls back to `getDashboardRoleUser()` when there is no session; `lib/currentUser.js:9` keeps the role in `globalThis.__CURRENT_USER__`; every web login calls `setCurrentRole` (`app/actions/auth.js:92,111,138`), so the last web Teacher login makes every cookie-less request a Teacher. That fallback actor has no `schoolId`. Live, no cookie: `GET /api/iam/me` returned a Teacher user, `/api/exams`, `/api/classes/sections-map`, `/api/subjects`, `/api/notices` returned 200, and `GET /api/support/tickets` returned ticket objects (including `ticketNumber`, `schoolId`) because `getSchoolTickets(undefined)` (`lib/support.js` where `{schoolId: undefined}`) applies no filter, i.e. tickets of ALL schools (`app/api/support/tickets/route.js`, `lib/support.js getSchoolTickets`).
Impact: unauthenticated cross-tenant read of support tickets (subjects, messages, names, attachment URLs); unauthenticated access to every route that only checks `if (!actor)`. State depends on which role last logged in on that server instance, so it is intermittent in serverless but permanent on a long-lived instance.
Recommendation: remove the dashboard-toggle branch from `getCurrentUserInfo` (return `null` when `getSession()` is empty); delete `lib/currentUser.js` global state or confine it to a dev flag; in `getSchoolTickets` and similar helpers throw if `schoolId` is falsy.
Theme: T1 Identity fallback and global tenant singleton

Title: POST /api/schools has no authentication and repoints the global active-school singleton
Evidence: `app/api/schools/route.js:21-53` — no `requireSuperAdmin` (only the `GET` at line 7 has it). It calls `addSchoolFromWizard` (`lib/schools.js:120`, creates a School), then `setActiveSchoolContext(school)` (`lib/school.js`, mutates `globalThis.__ACTIVE_SCHOOL__`) and `addSession`/`setActiveSession`.
Impact: anyone can create tenants (code collision probing, junk rows) and repoint the instance's fallback school, which affects the cron job, SuperAdmin sessions and API-001 actors for all later requests on that instance.
Recommendation: `const { error } = await requireSuperAdmin(); if (error) return error;` at the top; pass the new school id explicitly to session creation instead of mutating the singleton.
Theme: T1 Identity fallback and global tenant singleton

Title: Five handlers have no auth check on any path (fee ledger, create-order, verify, attendance by student, subjects GET)
Evidence: ledger `route.js:5-18` only blocks a Parent for a different child, never 401s on null; `create-order/route.js:11-17` and `verify/route.js:11-17` run the ownership check only when `actor?.role === 'Parent'`, otherwise proceed; `attendance/student/[id]/route.js:20-22` same pattern; `subjects/route.js:11`. Contrast the sibling `fees/student/[studentId]/route.js` which was fixed.
Impact: payment history and attendance of any student readable without login; unauthenticated Razorpay order creation (creates PENDING Payment rows and live Razorpay orders: abuse/spam); unauthenticated verify.
Recommendation: use `requireParent`/`requirePermission('fees.view')` or at minimum `if (!actor) 401` plus ownership check for any non-admin role; add a shared `requireActor()` helper.
Theme: T2 Missing or wrong authorization on routes, pages and libs

Title: Roles/permissions are global (not per tenant); any holder of permissions.manage edits roles for all schools
Evidence: `prisma Role` has `key @unique` and no `schoolId` (`schema.prisma:70-82`); `app/api/roles/[id]/permissions/route.js` replaces `RolePermission` rows of that single global role; `prisma/rbacPermissions.js:98` gives `PRINCIPAL = ALL_KEYS` which includes `permissions.manage` (`:70`).
Impact: a Principal of school A can change what Admin/Teacher/Accountant may do in every other school (including granting themselves nothing more, but revoking fees access platform-wide, or giving Teachers `students.delete`).
Recommendation: restrict `permissions.manage` to SuperAdmin, or make roles per-school. **Effort:** S (restrict) / L (per-school)
Theme: T1 Identity fallback and global tenant singleton

Title: Student documents (birth cert, Aadhaar, SLC) uploaded to a public-read R2 prefix with predictable keys
Evidence: `lib/storage.js:20-26` (public URL, comment requires public-read bucket); `app/api/students/document-upload-url/route.js:28` key = `students/<schoolId>/documents/<Date.now()>-<safeName>`; `app/api/support/upload-url/route.js:33` same pattern; `route.js:19-25` size/type trusted from the client.
Impact: identity documents of minors/parents are readable by anyone who obtains or guesses the URL (millisecond timestamp plus a usually predictable filename such as `aadhaar.pdf`); the URL is persisted and returned to every client that renders the student. No access revocation or audit is possible; deleting a student does not necessarily delete the object. This is a privacy/regulatory exposure (India's DPDP Act for children's data).
Recommendation: minimum: add `crypto.randomUUID()` to every key. Better: keep sensitive prefixes (`students/*/documents/`, Aadhaar) in a private bucket and serve through an authenticated route that returns a short-lived presigned GET (`@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner` is already installed). Also pass `ContentLength` via a presigned POST policy or re-check the object size with `HeadObject` on confirm.
Theme: T4 Identity documents and personal data exposure

Title: Fee-generation cron processes one school only (global singleton), and fails open if CRON_SECRET is unset
Evidence: `lib/fees.js:583-607` `generateDueStudentFees` calls `getFeeStructures()` which resolves the school via `resolveSchoolId()` (`lib/fees.js:217`) with no session, i.e. the global singleton (`lib/school.js`, defaults to a seed id). `app/api/cron/generate-fees/route.js:12-15` and `cleanup-support-tickets/route.js` only check the bearer when `process.env.CRON_SECRET` is set (fail-open).
Impact: in a multi-school deployment only one school gets auto-generated fees; the rest silently never do. If the secret is missing the endpoints are publicly callable (mass generation / ticket purge).
Recommendation: loop `prisma.school.findMany({status:'Active'})` and pass `schoolId` into every lib call; return 500 when `CRON_SECRET` is unset.
Theme: T5 Scheduled jobs (cron) are single-tenant and fail open

Title: No Razorpay webhook; verification relies on the browser callback; abandoned checkouts lose captured payments
Evidence: no `webhook` route exists under `app/api`; `lib/fees.js:1186-1193` comment acknowledges it. `verifyRazorpayPayment` (`lib/fees.js:1194-1265`) is reached only from the client POST.
Impact: if the parent's browser/app closes, loses network, or the callback fails after Razorpay captures money, the Payment row stays PENDING forever (no cleanup job, comment at `lib/fees.js:1142`) and the fee stays unpaid: money taken, school sees no payment. No reconciliation job either.
Recommendation: add `app/api/payments/razorpay/webhook/route.js` verifying `X-Razorpay-Signature` over the raw body with the school's webhook secret, resolving the Payment by `razorpayOrderId`, and reusing one shared `applySuccessfulPayment(paymentId)` that is idempotent and runs in a transaction with a conditional update (`updateMany where status:'PENDING'`).
Theme: T3 Online payment and fee integrity

Title: Online/manual payment races and overpayment: stale read, absolute write, many PENDING orders per fee, no cap
Evidence: `collectManualPayment` (`lib/fees.js:1025-1081`) reads the fee, computes `newPaidAmount = fee.paidAmount + collectAmount` in JS and writes it as an absolute value; no row lock, no idempotency key. `verifyRazorpayPayment` (`fees.js:1239-1251`) does the same with `payment.amount`, never re-checking that the amount is still owed. `createRazorpayOrder` (`fees.js:1147`) creates a new PENDING order on every call with no reuse or cap.
Impact: (1) two concurrent manual collections both pass the `<= remainingDue` check, create two Payment rows, but `paidAmount` is overwritten with one value (ledger sum greater than `paidAmount`); (2) a parent who opened two checkouts, or paid online after an admin collected cash, can have both verified: `paidAmount` exceeds payable, status PAID, no refund path (BIZ-005); (3) double-click on collect creates duplicate Payments.
Recommendation: use atomic updates: `prisma.studentFee.updateMany({ where: {id, schoolId, paidAmount: fee.paidAmount}, data:{ paidAmount: {increment: amt}}})` inside the transaction and abort on `count===0`; in verify re-compute remaining due and reject/flag overpay; reuse an existing PENDING order for the same fee; accept an `Idempotency-Key` on `/api/fees/collect`.
Theme: T3 Online payment and fee integrity

Title: Attendance lock rules are disabled in code; markedBy and records are client-controlled
Evidence: `lib/attendance.js:103-110` `ATTENDANCE_LOCK_ENABLED = false` makes `computeAttendanceAccess` always allow; the manual unlock (`manuallyUnlocked`, `attendance/[id]/lock`) therefore has no effect. `app/api/attendance/route.js` passes the raw body to `saveAttendance` (`lib/attendance.js:57`), which upserts `markedBy` (client supplied, `DailyAttendanceBoard.jsx:202`) and `records` (no schema check: statuses, studentIds belonging to the class, duplicates). Only Sunday is rejected; school calendar holidays and future dates are accepted.
Impact: a Teacher can alter any past or future date for their class, forge `markedBy`, and write arbitrary JSON into `records`, corrupting reports. Concurrent submissions are last-write-wins via the `[school, session, date, class, section]` unique upsert (no duplicate rows, which is good).
Recommendation: turn the flag on (or delete the dead matrix and decide the policy), derive `markedBy` from the session, validate `records` against the roster and `ATTENDANCE_STATUSES`, reject future dates.
Theme: T12 Business-rule gaps in exams, attendance, promotion and notifications

Title: Migration history does not represent the schema (1 init migration, 2 of 52 models)
Evidence: `prisma/migrations/20260830172048_init/migration.sql:1-38` creates only the `AdminStatus` enum and the `SuperAdmin` and `SchoolAdmin` tables; `prisma/schema.prisma` defines 52 models. `git log -- prisma/migrations` shows only the initial commit. `_prisma_migrations` in the local DB has exactly one row. `package.json:7` build script is `prisma generate && next build` (no `prisma migrate deploy`). The schema header comments and the existence of RBAC/support/enrollment tables in the local DB prove the schema was applied some other way (`db push` style).
Impact: A new environment (staging, DR restore target, a second region) cannot be created from the repo; `prisma migrate deploy` would produce a database missing 50 tables. No reviewable, reversible record of schema change; no safe path for additive changes with data (e.g. converting date strings to DateTime). Production schema drift cannot be detected.
Recommendation: Baseline: generate a full-schema migration from the production-equivalent schema (`prisma migrate diff --from-empty --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --script`), mark it applied on existing databases with `prisma migrate resolve --applied`, and from then on use `migrate dev`/`migrate deploy` in the release process.
Theme: T7 No tests, no CI, no reproducible migrations or recovery

Title: Manual fee collection is a read-modify-write outside the transaction: double-collect / overpay race
Evidence: `lib/fees.js:1025-1058` (`collectManualPayment`): reads the fee with `getStudentFeeById`, checks `status === 'PAID'` and `remainingDue` in JS, computes `newPaidAmount = fee.paidAmount + collectAmount`, then runs `$transaction([payment.create, studentFee.update({ paidAmount: newPaidAmount })])`. The transaction does not re-read or lock the fee, and `paidAmount` is written as an absolute value. `lib/fees.js:1194-1250` (`verifyRazorpayPayment`) has the same shape (`fee.paidAmount + payment.amount`). There is no unique key or CHECK constraint tying `sum(Payment.amount where SUCCESS)` to `StudentFee.paidAmount` or capping it at the payable amount (schema `StudentFee`, `Payment`, lines 537-557 and 1427-1443).
Impact: Two accountants (or a double click, or a manual collect racing a pending Razorpay verify for the same fee) both pass the "not PAID" check; two SUCCESS Payment rows are created while `paidAmount` reflects only one (or a Razorpay verify adds on top of a manual full payment). Ledger and fee row then disagree; the school's reconciliation breaks and parents can be double-charged. Local DB: fee rows are currently consistent (0 overpaid), so this is a latent defect, not observed corruption.
Recommendation: Inside one interactive transaction do the guarded update: `updateMany({ where: { id, schoolId, paidAmount: fee.paidAmount }, data: { paidAmount: { increment: amount }, status } })` and abort if `count === 0`; or `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` via `$queryRaw`. For Razorpay mark the pending Payment SUCCESS with `updateMany({ where: { id, status: 'PENDING' } })` first and only continue if it matched.
Theme: T3 Online payment and fee integrity

Title: Login identity is looked up by email only, but uniqueness is per school (or absent): ambiguous account resolution
Evidence: Schema: `Teacher` has no unique on `loginEmail` or `email` (only `@@unique([schoolId, employeeId])`, `schema.prisma:678`); `ParentAccount` is `@@unique([schoolId, email])` (285); `User` is `@@unique([schoolId, email])` (153); `SchoolAdmin.email` is globally unique (322-326). Lookups: `lib/teachers.js:436-440` and `:460-463` `findFirst({ where: { loginEmail: ... } })` with no school; `lib/parentAccounts.js:108-111` `findFirst` by email only; `lib/rbac.js:44-49` `user.findFirst` by email for Principal/Accountant. Local DB: one group of 4 teachers in one school shares the same `loginEmail` (demo data), 13 of 26 teachers have login enabled.
Impact: Two schools can legitimately register the same parent or teacher email (the schema permits it), after which `findFirst` returns an arbitrary row: the person logs into the wrong tenant, or a correct password for school B fails because school A's row was returned first (a person who is a parent at two schools cannot sign in to one). Within a school, duplicate teacher login emails make password-reset and login nondeterministic. This is both an integrity and a tenant-isolation risk (credential of one tenant matched against another tenant's account when passwords coincide).
Recommendation: Decide the product rule. Simplest consistent option: login emails are globally unique across tenants (unique index on lowercased email per identity table, or a single `User` identity table), with a data-cleanup migration first. Alternative: require a school code at login and look up `{ schoolId, email }`. Add `@@unique([schoolId, loginEmail])` to Teacher at minimum.
Theme: T9 Weak data model: string references, JSON arrays, duplicated sources of truth

Recommendation: Gate with __DEV__, delete/rotate seeded accounts in production

Title: Daily fee-generation cron only processes one fallback school, not every school
Evidence: `generateDueStudentFees()` calls `getFeeStructures()` (no school argument); that resolves school through `resolveSchoolId()`, which with no session (a cron has none — the function's own comment at `fees.js:579-583` says so) returns the process-wide `getActiveSchoolId()` singleton (`schoolContext.js:26`, default seed id at `lib/school.js:5,17`).
Impact: On a multi-school deployment the daily job generates term fees for at most one school (whichever the instance last "stepped into", else the seed id); all others are silently skipped while the route returns `success: true`. Parents of other schools are not billed on time; no one is alerted.
Recommendation: In the cron, `const schools = await prisma.school.findMany({select:{id:true}})` and call a school-parameterised generator for each, collecting per-school success/failure in the response.
Theme: T5 Scheduled jobs (cron) are single-tenant and fail open

Title: No Razorpay webhook or reconciliation; paid-but-unrecorded payments possible
Evidence: only `create-order` and `verify` routes exist under `app/api/payments/` (directory listing); `lib/fees.js:1191,1257` comments say a webhook is a future addition ("once built"). Payment rows start `PENDING` (`schema.prisma:1437`) and become `SUCCESS` only when the browser/app calls `verify` (`fees.js:1236-1248`). No job re-queries Razorpay for stale `PENDING` rows, and no admin screen lists them. Also `create-order/route.js:13` and `verify/route.js:12` skip the ownership check when no actor is signed in.
Impact: If a parent pays and the app/tab closes, the network drops, or the callback fails, money is captured at Razorpay but the fee stays unpaid and the Payment stays `PENDING` indefinitely; staff must reconcile manually against the Razorpay dashboard. Refunds do not exist either (prior audit P28). The null-actor path lets an unauthenticated caller create orders/PENDING rows against any fee id (signature check still protects `verify`).
Recommendation: Add `POST /api/payments/razorpay/webhook` (verify `X-Razorpay-Signature` with the webhook secret over the raw body; call the existing idempotent confirm path which already tolerates duplicates, `fees.js:1256-1262`), plus a daily/admin "stale PENDING payments" check that fetches the order status. Require a signed-in actor on `create-order`/`verify`.
Theme: T3 Online payment and fee integrity

Impact: Broken or insecure code deploys unchecked; about 100 uncommitted modified files obscure release provenance.

Title: Parent and Accountant roles can read any student's full record (Aadhaar, guardians, address)
Evidence: `app/api/students/[id]/route.js:7-19` — gate is `requirePermission('students.view')` followed by a block that rejects only `user.roleKey === 'Teacher'`; the comment (lines 10-16) states the route is meant to be "admin-tier only". `prisma/rbacPermissions.js` grants `students.view` to Parent (line ~205) and Accountant (line 195) as well as Teacher/Admin. `lib/students.js:310-312` returns the full decorated record by `{id, schoolId}`, i.e. including `aadhaarNumber`, guardian/secondary guardian (phones, emails, Aadhaar), address, documents URLs (schema `Student` 372-405).
Impact: A signed-in parent can fetch any other student in the same school (ids are cuids, but they are exposed in rosters, notices, links) and read minors' Aadhaar numbers, guardian contacts and addresses. Accountant (no teaching/admin need) gets the same. Same-school only; no cross-tenant leak.
Recommendation: In the route, allow only roles that legitimately need the full record: `if (!['Admin','Principal','SuperAdmin'].includes(user.roleKey)) return 403`; Parent already has dedicated parent routes. Consider returning a reduced projection for Accountant.
Theme: T2 Missing or wrong authorization on routes, pages and libs

Title: Aadhaar and identity documents stored under permanent unsigned public URLs
Evidence: `lib/storage.js:20-27` — `buildPublicUrl` returns `${R2_PUBLIC_URL}/${key}` and its comment states the bucket must allow public reads; there is no signed-GET path in the file. Student document keys are `students/<schoolId>/documents/<Date.now()>-<sanitised original filename>` (`students/document-upload-url/route.js:26-28`); teacher equivalent `teachers/document-upload-url/route.js:22-24`. The URL is stored in the DB (`Student.aadhaarDocumentUrl` schema 383, Teacher 629) and returned to API callers (see PRV-001).
Impact: Anyone holding or guessing a URL can download a child's or teacher's Aadhaar/birth-certificate scan with no authentication, no expiry and no access log. Keys are not high-entropy (millisecond timestamp plus a user-chosen filename such as the document type), and URLs leak through any log, referrer, shared screenshot or the PRV-001 route.
Recommendation: Smallest change: keep photos public, but store identity documents under a separate private bucket (no public domain) with a random key (`crypto.randomUUID()`), and serve them via a permission-checked route that returns a short-lived presigned GET (`GetObjectCommand` + `getSignedUrl`, 60-300 s). Existing objects need migration.
Theme: T4 Identity documents and personal data exposure

Title: Any signed-in Parent (and Accountant) can write homework and exam marks: routes only require a non-null actor and libs treat every non-Teacher as admin
Evidence: lib/examMarks.js:32-33,164-169,243-247; lib/homework.js:201-203,231-232,269-281; app/api/homework/route.js:21-47; app/api/exams/schedules/[scheduleId]/marks/route.js:33-52; app/api/homework/[id]/route.js:5-28 (code-based, not executed)
Impact: A parent token (mobile login) can POST/PUT/DELETE homework for any class (with push fan-out to students), read a full class marks sheet and upsert marks for any studentId. Academic-record integrity and spam of every parent in the school.
Recommendation: Replace the "role !== Teacher => allow" shortcut with explicit allow-lists (SchoolAdmin/SuperAdmin) and add requirePermission (marks.enter/marks.update, homework manage) at the route; add a negative test per role.
Theme: T2 Missing or wrong authorization on routes, pages and libs

Title: Dashboard server pages have no server-side role/permission guard: a signed-in Teacher can render Teachers, Fees, Settings and Promote pages with SSR data
Evidence: app/dashboard/teachers/[id]/page.jsx:15-18; app/dashboard/teachers/page.jsx:14-18; app/dashboard/fees/payments/page.jsx:9; app/dashboard/fees/students/page.jsx:15-31; app/dashboard/layout.jsx:10-17; middleware.js:26-30,86-94 (middleware only checks role tier). Not executed.

Evidence: app/actions/auth.js:76-77,92,100-101,111,138; lib/school.js:29-31,43-45; lib/auth/schoolContext.js:23-27; app/api/schools/[id]/manage/route.js:21-24

Recommendation: Remove active-school and dashboard-role singletons; carry the managed schoolId inside the SuperAdmin token or a per-request header validated server-side; resolveSchoolId must throw when no schoolId.

Title: No server-side schema validation; client-only zod; malformed JSON gives 500
Evidence: `lib/schemas.js` (zod, 659 lines) is imported only by client components (e.g. `components/fees/CollectFeeModal.jsx`); no `app/api` route imports it. 110 `await request.json()` calls, 0 with `.catch`; 36 route files have no `try` at all, and in most others `request.json()` sits before the `try`. Validation is `if (!field)` checks. Content-Type is not checked. Mass assignment is limited: `buildStudentFields`/`fieldsFrom` whitelist fields (no raw body spread into prisma found; only server-built `...data` in `examMarks.js:255`, `examSchedules.js:227`).
Impact: bad bodies return 500 with a stack in logs; numeric fields (`amount`, `marksObtained`, `maxMarks`) can be strings, NaN, fractional or negative until a lib check catches them.

Title: Unbounded list responses and unbounded request arrays
Evidence: `GET /api/students` returns the full decorated school (`app/api/students/route.js`), for Teachers it loads all students then filters in JS; `GET /api/users`, `GET /api/notices`, `GET /api/homework`, `GET /api/support/tickets`, `GET /api/subjects`, `getPaymentLedger`; `POST bulk-collect` `studentIds`, `students/bulk-import` `rows`, `exams/schedules/.../marks` `rows` and `fees/send-reminder` `studentIds` have no length cap. Paged variants exist for students, teachers, notices, homework, payments (page size capped at 50/100), but `payments` and `schools` do not cap `pageSize`.
Recommendation: cap array lengths (e.g. 500) and `pageSize`; migrate remaining list consumers to the paged routes. **Effort:** S–M
Theme: T8 Performance and scalability of data loads

Title: Upload presign does not bind size; free-form attachmentUrl/photoUrl stored; cleanup cron can delete another tenant's R2 object
Evidence: 13 `*upload-url` routes (list: students photo/document, teachers photo/document, school logo, admin/parent/teacher profile photo, notices, support). All require auth and allow-list `fileType`; keys are prefixed by `schoolId` (profile photos by user id) plus a sanitized name. But size is a client-stated `fileSize` only; `getPresignedUploadUrl` (`lib/storage.js`) signs `ContentType` but no `ContentLength`/size condition, so the real size is unlimited; no virus or magic-byte check; URLs are public (`R2_PUBLIC_URL`). `attachmentUrl` (support tickets/replies, `lib/support.js:111,130`) and `photoUrl` (self-profile PATCH) are stored without checking they point to this tenant's key prefix; `cleanupOldTickets` (`lib/support.js:229-232`) deletes whatever R2 key such a URL maps to.
Impact: storage abuse; a school user can reference another school's R2 object in a ticket and have it deleted by the cron after 90 days; arbitrary external URL rendered as a link.
Recommendation: validate `attachmentUrl`/`photoUrl` start with `R2_PUBLIC_URL + '/<prefix>/<schoolId>/'`; use a presigned POST with `content-length-range`. **Effort:** S–M
Theme: T12 Business-rule gaps in exams, attendance, promotion and notifications

Title: Rate limiting exists only on logins and is in-memory per instance
Evidence: `lib/auth/loginRateLimit.js` is an in-memory `Map` (per instance, reset on cold start), used by login/reset routes only. No limit on create-order, upload-url, support tickets, bulk endpoints, or fee collection.
Recommendation: a shared store (Upstash/Postgres) for login; per-user caps on order creation and ticket creation. **Effort:** M
Theme: T10 Session lifecycle, brute force and credential handling

Title: No Razorpay webhook: payment recording depends on the browser returning to the verify endpoint
Evidence: `app/api/payments/razorpay/` contains only `create-order/route.js` and `verify/route.js`; `lib/fees.js:1194-1265` `verifyRazorpayPayment` is idempotent (SUCCESS short-circuit at ~1214, unique `razorpayPaymentId` P2002 handling at ~1257-1262) but only runs when the client calls it; the comment at 1257 anticipates a webhook "once built".
Impact: if a parent pays and the app/browser dies, loses network, or the tab closes before `verify`, Razorpay captured the money while the `Payment` row stays `PENDING` and the fee stays unpaid. Schools see disputes and manual reconciliation. Double-submit safety is good; lost-callback safety is absent.
Recommendation: add `app/api/payments/razorpay/webhook/route.js` (raw body, `X-Razorpay-Signature` HMAC with a per-school webhook secret, handle `payment.captured`/`order.paid`), reusing the existing idempotent finalize logic from `verifyRazorpayPayment`. Add a nightly reconcile of PENDING payments older than 30 min via Razorpay `orders.fetchPayments`.
Theme: T3 Online payment and fee integrity

Title: No refund/reversal path; no collector or actor recorded on payments and discounts
Evidence: permission `fees.refund` exists (`prisma/rbacPermissions.js:128`) but no handler uses it; `Payment` model (`schema.prisma:1427`) has no `collectedBy`, `reference`, `receiptNo`, `refundedAt`; `applyFeeDiscount` blocks discounts below paid amount ("process a refund first", `fees.js:870`) yet no refund exists. Discount apply/remove, fee delete and collections write no audit row (exams have `logExamAudit`, fees do not).
Impact: wrong or duplicate collections cannot be reversed in-app; no answer to "who collected or discounted this".
Recommendation: add `Payment.collectedById/collectedByName`, a `FeeAuditLog` model written in the same transaction, and a `POST /api/fees/payments/[id]/reverse` gated by `fees.refund`. **Effort:** M–L - Money handling: `Int` rupee columns (no floats), PERCENT discount rounded with `Math.round`, late fee computed on read (`lateFeeAmountFor`) so `payableAmount` drifts upward daily while `status` was set PAID earlier with a fixed `paidAmount` (BIZ-003 side effect); manual amounts like `10.5` would raise a Prisma Int error returned as 400 with raw message.
Theme: T3 Online payment and fee integrity

Title: Marks edits after approval/publish do not invalidate or recompute results; marks save is non-transactional
Evidence: `saveExamMarks` (`lib/examMarks.js:164-258`) for an admin overwrites `status` with `Draft`/`Submitted` on rows that were `Approved`/`Published` (`:247`) and does not touch `ExamResult`; results are only recomputed when an admin runs generate manually (`examResults.js:113`). Upserts run one by one without a transaction (`:240-258`), so a failure leaves a partly saved sheet. `row.studentId` is not checked against the schedule roster. Max marks are checked at save time but `updateExamSchedule` can lower `maxMarks`/`passingMarks` later with no re-validation. `generateExamResults` re-upsert resets `status` to `Draft` (`:207`), un-publishing results parents already saw.
Recommendation: when a mark of a published exam changes, flag the student's `ExamResult` stale (or recompute) and keep status; wrap the row loop in `$transaction`; validate studentIds against the roster. **Effort:** M
Theme: T12 Business-rule gaps in exams, attendance, promotion and notifications

Title: Missing indexes: no schoolId-leading index on Payment, StudentFee, Notice, CalendarEvent; unindexed FK columns
Evidence: `pg_indexes` (local DB) and schema. Query patterns from `lib/*.js` vs index: - Students list/roster by `(schoolId, academicSession, class, section, status)`: `Students_schoolId_academicSession_class_section_status_idx` present. Good. Searches (`contains`, insensitive, on names/admissionId, `guardian` JSON path, `lib/students.js:268-286`) cannot use it beyond `schoolId`. - Attendance by date/class: unique `(schoolId, academicSession, date, className, sectionName)` serves day and date-range lookups. Good. Dashboard trend `WHERE schoolId` scans all rows of the school (see PERF-003). - Payments by school/status/date (`lib/fees.js:704-720`, `1408-1416`, `1537`, `1551`, `lib/dashboard.js:342`): the only indexes on `Payment` are the two `razorpay*` uniques. No `(schoolId, status, paidAt)` / `(schoolId, createdAt)` index; `Payment.studentId` and `Payment.studentFeeId` (FKs, used by ledger and fee detail) are unindexed. - StudentFee by school (`loadSchoolFees`, `lib/fees.js:1340`; groupBy at `:1413`): only `(studentId, academicSession, term)` unique exists; no `schoolId`-leading index. Local `EXPLAIN` of the payments query uses a Seq Scan (tiny table, not conclusive). - Notices (`lib/notices.js:58`), CalendarEvents (`lib/calendarEvents.js:40`), Subjects/Classes lists: filtered on `schoolId` with `orderBy createdAt/startDate`; Notice and CalendarEvent have no index at all. - Per-student lookups with no student-leading index: `ParentStudentLink(studentId)` (used by notification fan-out and fees, `lib/notices.js:477`, `lib/fees.js:996`; only `(parentAccountId, studentId)` unique exists), `ExamMark(studentId)`, `ExamResult(studentId)` (`lib/examResults.js:245`), `StudentEnrollments(classId)`, `(sectionId)`, `Sections(classTeacherId)`, `TeacherLeave(teacherId)`, `SubjectTests(teacherId, subjectId)`. - Postgres does not index FK columns automatically, so the cascades in DB-005 (delete Student) and Class/Section/Teacher deletes also seq-scan the child tables.
Impact: Fine at demo size. At the stated target (hundreds of thousands of payments, millions of ExamMarks, ParentNotifications growing with every notice x student) these become sequential scans shared across all tenants, plus slow deletes. Not a proven bottleneck; marked P2 because the fix is cheap and the table with highest write volume (Payment, ParentNotifications) lacks school-leading access paths.
Recommendation: `@@index([schoolId, status, paidAt])` and `@@index([studentId])`, `@@index([studentFeeId])` on Payment; `@@index([schoolId, academicSession])` on StudentFee; `@@index([schoolId, createdAt])` on Notice; `@@index([schoolId, startDate])` on CalendarEvent; `@@index([studentId])` on ParentStudentLink, ExamMark, ExamResult; `@@index([classId])`/`[sectionId]` on StudentEnrollment. Consider `pg_trgm` GIN indexes if student search becomes slow.
Theme: T8 Performance and scalability of data loads

Title: Hard delete of a Student cascades away exam results, marks, enrollment history and the "append-only" promotion log
Evidence: `lib/students.js:673-698` `deleteStudent` runs `prisma.student.delete`; it only fails (P2003) if StudentFee/Payment/MonthlyReport/YearlyReport/SubjectTestMark rows exist (Restrict). `pg_constraint` (local DB) and schema show Cascade from Student to `ExamMark`, `ExamResult`, `ExamOptionalEnrollment`, `StudentEnrollment`, `StudentPromotionLog`, `ParentNotification`, `ParentStudentLink`. `schema.prisma:1036-1040` documents `StudentPromotionLog` as "append-only ... never updated/deleted". The student's id also stays inside `Attendance.records` JSON.
Impact: A student who has exam marks and results but no fee row (e.g. fees not generated, or a school not using the fee module) can be hard-deleted, silently deleting published results, enrollment history and the promotion log (data a school is typically required to retain). Which students are deletable depends on an unrelated module's data. No soft-delete column exists; `status` TransferredOut/Graduated is the workaround and is advisory only. All 20+ `School` relations are Restrict, so a school cannot be offboarded/purged by a single delete and there is no documented tenant export/purge procedure.
Recommendation: Make delete = status change (or an `archivedAt DateTime?` column) for any student with enrollments/results; restrict hard delete to students with no academic or financial history; change `StudentPromotionLog.student` and `ExamResult.student` to Restrict.
Theme: T9 Weak data model: string references, JSON arrays, duplicated sources of truth

Title: All business dates are String; school timezone setting is never used to compute "today"
Evidence: `String` date columns: `Student.admissionDate`, `dob`; `Teacher.dob`, `joiningDate`, `relievingDate`; `Attendance.date`; `TeacherAttendance.date`; `Exam.startDate/endDate`; `ExamSchedule.examDate`; `FeeStructureTerm.startDate`; `AcademicSession.startDate/endDate`; `CalendarEvent.startDate/endDate`; `Notice.expiryDate`; `Homework.assignedDate`; `TeacherLeave.startDate/endDate`; `MonthlyReport.month`. Month filters use string prefixes (`lib/dashboard.js:101,109` `startsWith`), ranges rely on lexicographic order (`lib/attendance.js:174` `gte/lte` on strings). Local DB: all 163 attendance dates and 190 admission dates are well-formed 10-char values (no malformed data observed today). `lib/dateUtils.js:1-25` computes "today" from the server's local clock (`getFullYear/getMonth/getDate`), `lib/exams.js:128`, `lib/examMarks.js:413` use `toISOString().slice(0,10)` (UTC). `School.timezone` is saved (`lib/schoolSettings.js:151`) but grep finds no use of it in any date computation.
Impact: No DB-level validation (any string can be stored); correctness depends on every writer emitting `YYYY-MM-DD`. On Vercel the server clock is normally UTC, so for an Asia/Kolkata school between 00:00 and 05:30 local time "today" is the previous day: attendance "mark today", the 14:00 deadline (`School.attendanceDeadlineTime`, applied with server-local `setHours`), exam "upcoming/ongoing" and fee-term generation can act on the wrong day. Date arithmetic and reporting in SQL require casts.
Recommendation: Smallest effective step: one `schoolToday(timezone)` helper (using `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone })`) used by every "today" computation. Longer term, migrate date columns to `@db.Date` with a CHECK or a backfill migration (needs DB-001 first).
Theme: T9 Weak data model: string references, JSON arrays, duplicated sources of truth

Title: Attendance / assignments / timetable stored as JSON arrays of ids with no FK, no per-student uniqueness, last-writer-wins saves
Evidence: `Attendance.records` (`schema.prisma:874`), `TeacherAttendance.records` (723), `Teacher.assignments` (661), `TimeTable.schedule` (812), `Student.guardian/feeDetails/documents` (387-400), `CalendarEvent.appliesToClasses/Sections`, `GeneratedReportJob.targetIds String[]`. `lib/attendance.js:57-69` `saveAttendance` upserts the whole `records` array supplied by the client. Local DB orphan checks (all 0): attendance record ids not in Students; teacher assignments referencing a non-existent Class; notices pointing at missing teachers. 163 attendance rows hold 1,700 student marks (about 10 per row) in the demo data.
Impact: (a) Student/teacher ids inside JSON are never checked by the DB: deleting or transferring a student leaves dangling ids and a student can appear twice in one `records` array. (b) Concurrency: two users saving the same class+date (teacher plus admin override) overwrite each other (last writer wins, no version/`updatedAt` precondition). (c) Per-student attendance queries cannot use an index; every report scans and `find()`s inside arrays (PERF-009). (d) The design is a conscious trade-off (documented at `schema.prisma:852-862`), reasonable for write amplification, but it makes attendance the one core record without referential integrity. `Student.feeDetails` JSON duplicates fee concepts that also live in StudentFee (see REL-005).
Recommendation: Keep the row-per-section shape but (1) add an `updatedAt`/version precondition to `saveAttendance`, (2) validate that every `studentId` belongs to the section's enrolled roster before saving (one query), (3) when a student is removed, either block or purge ids from records. A row-per-student `AttendanceEntry(attendanceId, studentId, status)` table is the proper fix if per-student reporting becomes a hot path; benchmark first.
Theme: T9 Weak data model: string references, JSON arrays, duplicated sources of truth

Title: Aadhaar, PAN and bank details stored and served in plaintext
Evidence: `schema.prisma:376` (`Student.aadhaarNumber String`), guardian Aadhaar inside `guardian`/`secondaryGuardian` Json (`lib/students.js:319-333`), `Teacher.aadhaarNumber` (624), `panNumber` (634), `bankDetails Json` (637). `lib/auth/encryption.js` (AES-256-GCM) exists but is used only for the Razorpay key secret (`lib/razorpay.js:4`, `lib/schools.js:2`). `lib/teachers.js:103,110,119` return Aadhaar, PAN and bank details; `GET /api/teachers/paged` (`paged/route.js:18-27`) returns that full decorated shape for every teacher on every page to any holder of `teachers.view` (Admin/Principal).
Impact: A database leak, backup exposure or an over-broad read exposes government IDs and bank accounts directly; list views carry far more than a table needs.
Recommendation: (1) Return a list projection without Aadhaar/PAN/bank from `paged`; fetch sensitive fields only on a detail view. (2) Reuse `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret` for `aadhaarNumber`, `panNumber` and bank account number, and display masked (last 4) by default. Requires a one-off data migration; search by these fields is not currently offered.
Theme: T4 Identity documents and personal data exposure

Title: No erasure/retention path for student/teacher personal data and documents
Evidence: `deleteStudent` removes the row and only the profile photo object (`students.js:693-696`); Aadhaar, guardian and other document URLs in `documents`/`aadhaarDocumentUrl`/guardian Json are never deleted from R2. A student with any fee/payment row cannot be deleted at all (Restrict, `:686-690`); the suggested alternative is status change, which keeps all personal data. No teacher delete route exists (`app/api/teachers/[id]` has `assignments`, `reset-password`, `status`, `route.js` with PUT only). Only support tickets have a retention job (`lib/support.js:234-254`, 90 days). No data-export (access) function and no anonymisation function were found.
Impact: Personal data of children and staff persists indefinitely, and orphaned identity documents remain publicly reachable (PRV-002) even after a "delete". If the operator must honour deletion/withdrawal requests, there is no supported way to do it.
Recommendation: On delete/transfer-out purge document objects (`documents.*Url`, `aadhaarDocumentUrl`, guardian document URLs) via `deleteObject`; add an `anonymizeStudent` that blanks identifiers but keeps fee/payment rows; define a retention schedule with the school (fee records often have statutory retention — verify).
Theme: T4 Identity documents and personal data exposure

Title: No privacy notice, terms or consent capture anywhere (web and mobile)
Evidence: case-insensitive grep for privacy/consent/terms across `app` and `components` finds only fee-term wording; `schoolapp360/src` and `app.json` contain no privacy/consent references. Login pages, parent account creation (`lib/parentAccounts.js`) and student admission forms carry no notice or consent record; there is no consent field in `schema.prisma`.
Impact: The product processes data of minors (DOB, Aadhaar, caste, religion, blood group, guardian contacts). Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, personal data of persons under 18 generally requires verifiable parental/guardian consent and a notice; tracking/behavioural monitoring of children is restricted. Whether the school (data fiduciary) or SchoolApp360 (processor) must collect that here, and in what form, is a legal question; code alone shows no mechanism. Not a compliance conclusion. Mobile stores crash data via Sentry (see PRV-006); no ad/behavioural analytics SDKs were found in either `package.json`.
Recommendation: After legal advice: publish privacy notice/terms pages, link from login screens and app stores, add a recorded acceptance (timestamp, version) at parent first-login and a school-level data-processing agreement. Data minimisation: make caste/religion/Aadhaar optional per school.
Theme: T4 Identity documents and personal data exposure

Title: Money design: whole-rupee Int, derived payable amount, no DB invariants, hard-coded INR/paise
Evidence: All amounts are `Int` (`StudentFee.totalAmount/paidAmount`, `Payment.amount`, discounts, late fees); no Float/Decimal for money. `lib/fees.js:100-104` rounds percent discounts with `Math.round`; late fees accrue per day at read time (`discountAmountFor`, `lateFeeAmountFor`, `daysOverdueFor`), so `payableAmount` is never stored and changes as time passes. `lib/fees.js:1157,1166` hard-code `* 100` paise and `currency: 'INR'` while `School.currency` exists. No CHECK that `paidAmount <= payable` or `amount > 0`; no receipt number or refund/reversal row type (`PaymentStatus` has no REFUNDED); abandoned Razorpay orders stay PENDING forever (local DB: 9 PENDING vs 4 SUCCESS Razorpay payments).
Impact: Whole rupees are acceptable for Indian school fees but cannot represent paise-level concessions; the stored `status` (PAID) can become inconsistent with a later-changing computed payable amount; no audit-grade receipt sequence per school. Not a correctness bug today.
Recommendation: Add CHECK constraints (`paidAmount >= 0`, `amount > 0`); add a per-school receipt number on SUCCESS payments; freeze late fee into the StudentFee (or record it as a StudentFeeItem) when applied; add a PENDING-order expiry job. Keep Int but document the unit as rupees.
Theme: T3 Online payment and fee integrity

Title: DB-level invariants documented as "enforced in code" are not enforced (one active session, one class-teacher per session)

Impact: Concurrent requests or direct DB edits can violate them. Postgres partial unique indexes handle both: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON "AcademicSessions"("schoolId") WHERE status = 'Active'`; `ON "Sections"("classTeacherId","academicSession") WHERE "classTeacherId" IS NOT NULL`; `ON "User"(lower(email)) WHERE "schoolId" IS NULL`. Prisma cannot declare them but they can live in a migration (needs DB-001).
Theme: T9 Weak data model: string references, JSON arrays, duplicated sources of truth

Title: Child tables without schoolId (ReportLock cannot be tenant-scoped at all)
Evidence: Models without a `schoolId` column: `StudentFeeItem`, `FeeStructureTerm`, `FeeStructureItem`, `SubjectTestMark`, `MonthlyReportActivity/Holistic/Remark`, `SupportTicketReply` (all reachable only through a tenant-owned parent, acceptable), plus `ReportLock` (`schema.prisma:1648-1658`: polymorphic `reportId`, `userId` with no FK and no `schoolId`, so a tenant filter on it is impossible) and `SubjectTestMark.studentId` which is not tied to the test's school by any constraint. Global-by-design: `Role`, `Permission`, `RolePermission`, `SuperAdmin`. Per-school-scoped uniqueness exists for Student.admissionId, Teacher.employeeId, Class, Section (via class), Subject, Session, ParentAccount, User (nullable). `ParentStudentLink.schoolId` is denormalised but nothing enforces that it equals both sides' school (comment at `schema.prisma:288-294` admits it is app-checked).
Impact: Cross-tenant joins are blocked only by application code. ReportLock rows cannot be listed or purged per tenant.
Recommendation: Add `schoolId` + index to `ReportLock`; for the ParentStudentLink invariant use composite FKs `(schoolId, studentId)` -> `Student(schoolId, id)` (requires `@@unique([schoolId, id])` on Student and ParentAccount).
Theme: T9 Weak data model: string references, JSON arrays, duplicated sources of truth
